Elena — thanks for the redline and matrix. Looping in our privacy counsel Monica and our contracts lead Marissa to take point on the review. We can get you a detailed set of comments tomorrow EOD, but a couple of quick clarifying Qs to speed alignment:

1) Processing scope: your redline narrows "Purpose" language. Can you confirm whether Novanet needs an enterprise-specific processing clause (e.g., retention/split of logs) or if your redline is general?
2) Subprocessors: we typically give customers 30 days notice for new subprocessors and provide the list on request. If you require an approval model instead of notification, please call that out.
3) Data residency: please confirm any mandatory residency constraints for the account (we'll route to infra if there are regional lock requirements).

On e-sign: Redwood standard is DocuSign but we can accommodate AdobeSign for strategic enterprise deals. Please let us know which your procurement prefers and whether Novanet requires a countersignature by paper for records.

We will prepare a Redwood counter-redline with tracked changes and a short memo describing the open items.

Best,

Subject: RE: Novanet DPA - redlines (attached)

Team — I reviewed Novanet's redline. I drafted a prioritized list of issues and suggested language we should propose in a counter. Pulling out the high-risk items so we can decide positions before sending to Novanet: 

1) Definitions / Roles — Proposed: keep the core "Processor/Controller" language consistent with our Master Services Agreement. If Novanet insists on controller-to-controller treatment in parts, we need a carve for telemetry/usage data. Suggested clause: "Redwood will act as Processor of Customer Personal Data to the extent it processes such data on Customer's behalf in providing the API and related services."

2) Subprocessors — Acceptable: 30 days notice + right to object within 14 days for material concerns. Unacceptable: unilateral approval rights for every subprocessor. Proposed text: "Redwood will notify Customer of new subprocessors at least 30 days prior to onboarding; Customer may object on reasonable data protection grounds within 14 days; if not resolved, parties will escalate to senior legal contacts."

3) Audit rights — Novanet redline requests broad onsite audits. Counter: limit to remote audits or 1 onsite audit per 12 months, scoped and preceded by 30 days' notice; allow use of independent third party reports (SOC 2) in lieu of full audit where applicable. Proposed: "Customer may conduct one audit per 12 months, subject to scope and advance notice; Redwood may, at its discretion, satisfy audit obligations by providing up-to-date independent assurance reports and redacted evidence."

4) Liability cap & indemnities — Novanet attempts to carve out wider exceptions. We should preserve existing MSA cap; consider narrow exception for willful misconduct.

5) Cross-border transfers / SCCs — We should accept SCCs + UK addendum provided that (a) SCCs are attached (Novanet already provided matrix); (b) we reference our TOMs and commit to reasonable supplemental measures. Also confirm whether Novanet wants SCCs embedded in the executed DPA or exchanged as a separate annex.

6) Data retention / deletion — Ask for operational specifics if their retention needs differ from our default deletion workflows.

Attachments I will prepare: Redwood_counter_v1.docx (counter redline), Redwood_TOMs_summary.pdf (high-level technical and organizational measures), both to be shared with Novanet and copied into the HubSpot deal record.

Action items:
- Monica to finish counter-redline and proposed language (target: 5/13 AM).
- Neha to confirm e-sign vendor preference from Novanet and whether procurement requires AdobeSign.
- Marissa to validate we can meet any residency constraints and confirm SOC reports availability.

If Novanet insists on AdobeSign that is OK for this account; DocuSign remains our default. Recommend we propose DocuSign but accept AdobeSign if procurement pushes.

Monica Patel
Privacy Counsel | Redwood Inference

From: Elena Torres <elena.torres@novanet.com>

Subject: Re: Novanet DPA - redlines (attached)

Thanks Monica and team — appreciate the clear summary. A few clarifications from Novanet legal / procurement: 

- Audit: Novanet can accept the "1 onsite audit per 12 months" limitation provided Redwood agrees to allow reasonable scope and to provide necessary SOC2 / penetration test reports in advance.
- Subprocessors: 30 days notice is acceptable. Novanet prefers an approval right for subprocessors that will access production customer data (rather than blanket approval for any tooling). Can Redwood accept a narrow approval carve for subprocessors with production data access only?
- E-sign: procurement prefers AdobeSign for our internal workflow. If Redwood prefers DocuSign, Novanet is willing to accept DocuSign only if Redwood can host the executed contract in PDF form in our procurement system immediately after signing.

Cc'ing our outside counsel Alex Byrne for any legal follow-up. Please send your counter-redline and we'll mark up.

Thanks,
Elena
